note: Machine-readable registry of what is actually unsolved in this repo. Add an entry the moment something is found open; do not let it live only in prose. `kind` says what class of evidence would settle it, not how hard it is.

kinds.CODE: settled by a runnable implementation plus a falsifier
kinds.DERIVATION: settled by an argument from stated premises, checkable by computation
kinds.DEFINITION: settled by choosing and defending a definition; the gap is conceptual, not computational
kinds.BENCH: settled only by an instrument reading. Cost and instrument are named.

problems.title: What the physical anchor standard IS
problems.statement: The INSTRUMENT route asks whether a stability reference moved at the same timestamp as a residual. The mechanism is built: anchor_dev is a declared deviation against an explicit ANCHOR_TOL. What is not specified is the reference itself.
problems.why_open: It needs a standard whose failure mode does not correlate with the working sensors'. An anchor that drifts the same way as the sensor it checks is not an anchor.
would_count: A named physical reference per channel whose value is set by something other than the sensor electronics
An Allan-deviation curve for that reference, at rest, giving ANCHOR_TOL as a function of averaging time
A stated failure mode, and an argument that it is uncorrelated with the working sensor's

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: for a float sensor that means 'any nonzero', which is always true

leads: Allan variance (Allan 1966; IEEE Std 952) separates white / flicker / random-walk drift by log-log slope
Dissimilar redundancy: sensors of different physical principle, so failure modes do not correlate
Analytical redundancy / parity space (Chow & Willsky 1984) needs no reference standard at all, only redundancy plus a model
Thermodynamically-fixed anchors: ice bath, saturated salt slurries (ASTM E104: LiCl 11.3% RH, MgCl2 33%, NaCl 75%), calibration mass, shorted/open input, Spectralon reflectance target
Westgard multi-rule QC has published error-detection and false-rejection rates per rule

problems.title: The conservation ledger: what is the reservoir, in what units
problems.statement: The spend ledger counts query cost and credits whether the funded query moved a claim. That is a budget with a yield, not a conservation law. Without a reservoir there is no way to state that the loop is not creating information from nothing.
problems.why_open: Units were never stated, so they were not guessed. Three candidate reservoirs exist and they are not the same quantity.
would_count: A named conserved quantity with units
A measurement procedure for it from the existing logs
A demonstration that the loop cannot increase it without an input
leads: Expected information gain (Lindley 1956), in bits or nats: KL from prior to posterior
Value of information (Howard 1966), units of whatever the decision pays in
Stochastic thermodynamics: Sagawa-Ueda; Parrondo, Horowitz & Sagawa 2015. Continuous with the Landauer work already in Negentropic/
Empowerment (Klyubin, Polani & Nehaniv 2005): channel capacity actuators -> sensors, in bits

problems.title: What a shape-level claim band IS
problems.statement: shape is documented canonical -- 'Do NOT scalarize on ingest' -- and no code path reads it. test() compares value only, so every claim in the system is a claim about one scalar projection.
problems.why_open: Storing the shape without testing against it is scalarizing with a receipt. A reading carrying a shape must now name its projection, which makes the loss explicit and auditable, but does not remove it. What a band on a vector, a spectrum, or a multi-axis reading should BE is a physics question.
would_count: A definition of 'inside the band' for a non-scalar reading that is not a norm in disguise
A signed residual for it, so the correlation branch still has something to correlate
A demonstration on a real multi-axis reading where the shape-level test and the scalar test disagree, and an argument for which is right

problems.title: Period estimation, and the scanned lag range
problems.statement: The slotted autocorrelation reports STRUCTURED with a calibrated p-value but refuses to name a period, because the argmax lag is not one: a rider peaks at every multiple of T/2 and noise picks the winner. Separately, a rider whose period exceeds n_slots*slot_width is invisible; lag_range_s is reported but nothing widens it.
problems.why_open: Both textbook autocorrelation handles were measured and both refused. Smallest-significant is always slot 1 because rho -> 1 as tau -> 0. First-local-minimum ran biased low and worsened with period: 7.5 s against a true 10.0.
would_count: A period estimate on irregularly sampled data with measured error against known riders
A false-alarm rate on white noise at a stated alpha
Stdlib only, no numpy

prior_attempts.why_it_failed: median 8.8 s against a true T/2 of 3.0 s on a Poisson clock
biased low, worsening with period: 7.5 s against a true 10.0 at T=20

leads: Lomb-Scargle (Lomb 1976; Scargle 1982); floating-mean generalisation (Zechmeister & Kuerster 2009)
CLEAN deconvolution of the spectral window (Roberts, Lehar & Dreher 1987)

problems.title: The exact binomial tail is discrete, and the conservatism costs power
problems.statement: The covariate gate uses an exact one-sided binomial tail. Because the distribution is discrete, the achieved level sits near 1% against a nominal 5%. That conservatism costs more power than the choice between Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg does.
problems.why_open: Measured but not fixed. Recovering the level is a known problem with known answers, none of which were implemented.
would_count: A gate whose achieved false-positive rate is close to the nominal alpha on the same nulls
Measured power gain against the current gate on the same real effect
No increase in false-positive rate
leads: mid-p correction
randomised / fuzzy decision at the boundary
Berger-Boos or similar

problems.title: MISSING_VARIABLE is correlational and cannot conclude
problems.statement: The branch tests whether residuals concentrate under a covariate. It is now correctly calibrated, and it still cannot distinguish a cause from a confounder.
problems.why_open: 'Concentrates under' is not 'is caused by'. With enough logged covariates something always concentrates, which the calibration fixes; it does not fix the inferential gap.
would_count: A conditional-independence test over the logged covariates, stdlib
A worked case where the marginal and conditional verdicts differ
An honest statement of what the loop can and cannot conclude from observational logging alone
leads: Peters, Janzing & Schoelkopf, Elements of Causal Inference (free online)
Simpson's paradox as the concrete failure

problems.title: Trajectory-level entropy production
problems.statement: Negentropic/ entropy production is a housekeeping estimator with a known sign bias. NEG-8 (persistence margin Phi = -S_exchange - sigma) cannot be evaluated on simulated traces until sigma is estimated at trajectory level.
would_count: A MaxCal or equivalent trajectory-level estimator
Sign-bias measured against a known-sigma simulation
Stdlib tier

problems.title: Two falsifiers implemented and never run against data
problems.statement: NEG-2 (archive lifetime under an expanding maintenance schedule) and NEG-3 (finite-time Landauer erasure, tau^-1 excess scaling) have runnable falsifiers and no data.
would_count: A dataset, its provenance, and the falsifier's verdict on it

problems.title: Derive the merit weights from something, or call it a mean
problems.statement: The five sovereignty criteria ship at 0.20 each. 77% of random reweightings reproduce the same high-merit rate, so the weights carry no information. evaluate_pattern now reports weights_are_flat alongside every score.
would_count: Weights derived from a stated procedure, not asserted
verdict_is_weight_sensitive() returning weights_carry_information = True on real patterns
Or: an argument that an unweighted mean is correct, in which case rename total_score

problems.title: Measure logical consistency instead of naming it unmeasured
problems.statement: _check_internal_coherence carried a flat 0.4 placeholder for logical consistency. The term was removed rather than guessed at, and logical_consistency is now listed in unmeasured_components.
would_count: A computable check over Pattern.mathematical_structure
Its own weight, stated
A pair of patterns it separates that the current two components do not

problems.title: Energy per bit has three values and they differ in legality
problems.statement: 1-2 aJ is 348 kT ln2 (legal). 0.1 eV is 5.6 kT ln2 (legal). 0.01 eV is 0.56 kT ln2, below the Landauer bound at 300 K.
problems.why_open: Pick one and propagate it through the documents that depend on it. 0.01 eV cannot be it.
would_count: One value, chosen with a stated basis
Every downstream figure recomputed
reach(E, 'landauer 300K') returning DETECTABLE

problems.title: Are 8 implant states separable at >3 sigma?
problems.statement: Eight doping states, measured as (sheet resistance, carrier type, carrier concentration). Separable at >3 sigma or not.
problems.why_open: Cheap, decisive, unrun. Needs no magnet, no cryostat, no THz source.
would_count: Measured (R_s, type, n) for 8 states with error bars
Pairwise separation in sigma
Cost and instrument named

problems.title: Piezoresistive dR/R at 0.1% strain
problems.statement: The strain channel that replaces every magnetic proposal predicts dR/R about 9% at 0.1% strain, gauge factor about 121 for pi_l along <110> paired with E<110> = 169 GPa.
problems.why_open: A strain gauge and a four-point probe settle it. Unrun.
would_count: Measured dR/R vs strain
Extracted gauge factor with the crystal direction stated
Agreement or disagreement with 121

problems.title: Bifilar common-mode rejection at achievable matching tolerance
problems.statement: The 60 dB common-mode suppression budget depends on a matching tolerance that was assumed, not measured.
would_count: Measured CMRR by magneto-optic sampling at a stated frequency
The matching tolerance actually achieved
Comparison against the budget in transient_suppression.py

problems.title: An n-dependent bit width against a fixed-width encoder contract
problems.statement: Negentropic/emit_ising.py does not inherit from bridges/abstract_encoder.py. The blocker is that an Ising spec has a bit width that depends on n, while every other encoder emits a fixed width.
would_count: A contract that admits both, or an argument that they are different kinds of thing and should not share one

problems.title: The Raman photon budget on the actual rig
problems.statement: The proposed architecture assumes a 1024-point spectrum on every acquisition, with a scheduler budgeting model frames per acquisition, for live imaging. A shot-noise budget at 785 nm / 10 mW / NA 1.2 / 25% throughput gives 30-300 s per spectrum at SNR 10 per channel, so the acquisition is the bottleneck by one to two orders and the scheduler is optimising the wrong resource.
problems.why_open: The estimate uses assumed cross-sections and scatterer densities. The rig's own number settles it and nothing else does.
would_count: Photons per channel per second measured on one unperturbed cell at the working power
The resulting seconds-per-spectrum at a stated SNR
The achievable frames per hour, which fixes n for every downstream model
leads: repo_guard.reach is the same comparison, already mechanised
Coherent Raman (SRS/CARS) buys 1e4-1e5 but is narrowband: sweeping 1024 points gives the time back
Broadband CARS buys ~1e2-1e3 against a worse nonresonant background

problems.title: False-alarm rate of a latent-space claim predicate
problems.statement: The example claim is `u[0] > 0.5 and u[1] < -0.2` with falsification after 3 consecutive failures. Nothing states the per-observation false-alarm rate on an unperturbed cell, so the stopping rule has no calibration.
problems.why_open: FCL-5 is the same shape: `rate > 1.5 x base` fired on 34-41% of null sets while its own notes said only 'too permissive'.
would_count: Technical replicates of one unperturbed cell
The predicate run against them, with the false-alarm count
A threshold set from that number rather than from inspection

problems.title: Does the manifold separate biochemistry, or batch structure?
problems.statement: 'The manifold learns to distinguish cell states.' Untested against a null in which the biochemistry is destroyed and the acquisition structure is kept.
would_count: The identical architecture trained on phase-randomised spectra, or on real spectra with shuffled state labels
Separation measured the same way in both
A stated margin between them
leads: repo_guard.null_harness
NEG-7 died exactly here

problems.title: A claim that survives retraining the encoder
problems.statement: A hypothesis written as `u[1] > 0.3` is a claim about one fitting run: retrain the encoder and the axes rotate. The latent is also learned from the same spectra the claim is tested on.
problems.why_open: This is P-SELF-SUPPLIED-FALSIFIER, the largest unmechanised shape in PRINCIPLES.json.
would_count: Claims stated in spectral terms -- a band, a ratio, a shift -- rather than latent coordinates
Or: a frozen encoder, a held-out split, and the claim written before the split is seen
A demonstration that the claim's verdict is unchanged across two independent training runs

problems.title: Full spectrum at minutes, or a few bands at video rate
problems.statement: The design assumes both a 1024-point spectrum and real-time acquisition. Spontaneous Raman gives the first; coherent Raman gives the second for one or a few shifts. No instrument gives both.
would_count: A stated choice, with the model redesigned for the n it implies
Or a named instrument that delivers both, with its throughput
